units.note: Numbers checked: 70,000 foot, 4,000 horse, 32 elephants; 3,000 and 500 from Colichas; 45,000 foot, 3,000 horse. All match.

findings.problem: Greek has Μασαννάσαν (accusative of Μασαννάσας, i.e. Masinissa); the English reproduces the Greek accusative ending as if it were part of the name.

findings.quote: he ordered the Iberians to keep advancing in the same formation.
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (***) after τὴν ἐπαγωγήν and then breaks off mid-sentence (τῷ μὲν δεξιῷ τὰς σημαίας καὶ τὰς ἴλας ἐπι-). The English reads as a complete sentence and hides both the gap and the truncation.
findings.proposed_fix: he ordered the Iberians to keep their ranks and make their advance in the same way [gap in the Greek text] ... the right wing, the standards and squadrons ... [the text breaks off here].

findings.quote: divided them behind the battle line between the two wings
findings.problem: Greek μερίσας ἐφ᾽ ἑκάτερον κέρας ὀπίσω τῶν παρατεταγμένων: he divided them to each wing, behind the line; not placed between the wings.
findings.proposed_fix: divided them, one part to each wing, behind the battle line

units.note: The chapter ends mid-sentence in the Greek and chapter 23 resumes mid-sentence.

findings.quote: and within each wing the infantry of the cavalry
findings.problem: Greek καὶ καθόλου τὸ δεξιὸν κέρας τῷ λαιῷ καὶ κατὰ μέρος οἱ πεζοὶ τοῖς ἱππεῦσιν: in general the right wing was the reverse of the left, and in particular the infantry the reverse of the cavalry. English leaves 'the infantry of the cavalry', which loses the contrast.
findings.proposed_fix: and, in detail, the infantry's movement was the reverse of the cavalry's

units.note: Chapter opens mid-sentence in the Greek (continuation of the break at the end of ch. 22); English begins as if whole.
The final fragment (Ilourgeia) is a separate excerpt in the Greek; English runs it on after the storm passage but does not misstate it.
The 'as though the money were being gathered' rendering of ὡς ... γινομένης τῆς παρασκευῆς is slightly interpretive but the ὡς-phrase is ambiguous; left alone.

findings.quote: When the tribunes had explained what had been decided
findings.problem: Greek has an explicit lacuna marker (...) between the first sentence (περὶ τὴν τῶν χρημάτων ἐπιμέλειαν) and τῶν δὲ χιλιάρχων διασαφούντων. English joins them seamlessly.
findings.proposed_fix: [gap in the Greek text] When the tribunes had explained what had been decided

findings.quote: prepare rations for a longer expedition within three days
findings.problem: Greek πρὸ ἡμερῶν τριῶν ἐφόδια παρεσκευάσθαι κατὰ πλείω χρόνον: provisions to be ready three days beforehand, for a longer time. 'Within three days' is not what πρὸ ἡμερῶν τριῶν says; the phrase is somewhat compressed.
findings.proposed_fix: have provisions prepared three days in advance, for a longer period
